Senekal 2 - A community on the edge

By: Graham Coetzer | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We visit the town of Senekal for the second court appearance of a group of suspects accused of a violent farm attack and murder - while tensions fly high between the farming community and the EFF.

Unique Selling Point:
Last week, Economic Freedom Fighters leader Julius Malema called on his "ground forces" to attend the next Senekal court appearance, to "defend" public property after protests by an angry farming community turned violent last tuesday. Farmers damaged court property and are accused of setting a police vehicle on fire. One of the farmers, Andre' Pienaar has since been arrested and denied bail. Amidst calls for calm from senior government officials, and a visit to murdered Brendin Horner's family by police minister Bheke Cele today, is enough being done to prevent what could easily become a bloodbath if the situation spirals out of control.

Summary:
We will be on the ground on friday, and film events as they happen. Hopefully the tensions will be eased, but it does seem like both sides are spoiling for a fight. We have obtained cellphone footage showing a large SANDF camp being erected near town. The idea is to produce a 4 minute insert telling the events of friday - and should all hell break loose we will be on scene.

Further information:
We will attempt to get an interview with the Horner family.

We will see who the main role players are on the day for comment.

We can get footage of Minister Cele's visit today.

Extra Budget Items:
I will travel with my own vehicle, and charge only for fuel used.

Script:


Seismic Senekal
17 Oct 2020
First Draft Script

PART 1

Voice
On friday this week the town of Senekal was once again the scene of chaos as a fed up farming community faced off with a large contingent of EFF supporters outside the magistrates court, where two of the men accused of 21 year old farmer Brendin Horner’s murder appeared for their ongoing bail application.

Link Derek
This is an idyllic Free State landscape, seemingly quiet and peaceful. But it’s right on this farm that a brutal murder sparked what has been called the battle of Senekal.

Voice
Gillie Scheepers owns the farm Bloukruin, where the 21 year old Horner, affectionately nicknamed Mr B, lived, worked and had his life cut so tragically short.

Sound Up Gillie
He had no enemies with the workers, everybody here, white black, everybody loved him.

Voice
Scheepers believes Horner stumbled across members of a stock theft syndicate - a problem he says that plagues the area, especially animals like sheep, which are easier to steal.

Sound Up Scheepers
Scheepers: 40, 50 kms around Paul Roux, nobody can farm with stock anymore, unless you’ve got your own reaction task force or whatever. And many of the black farmers have actually sold their sheep. They haven’t got any sheep. They still do try to farm with cattle, but sheep, not at all.

Derek: There’s a suspicion of police complicity when it comes to stock theft?

Scheepers: That could be, I mean there are many times that we report stock theft that the police don’t even rock up. They don’t even rock up.

Voice
Two weeks ago, Horner was attacked at this gate, just a few hundred meters from the house he shared with his girlfriend.

Sound Up Scheepers
Scheepers: He came down the road, and then up here, and then turned into his gate here.

Watts: And that’s where it happened?

Scheepers: And as I say that’s where the big fight was.

Voice
Pieces of the bakkie he was driving were found torn off the vehicle, and covered in both his and the perpetrators blood.

Sound Up Gillie
The body parts of the van were over there, I think the fight to took place here, his hat was over here.


Voice
The struggle continued across the road to where Horner, who put up a valiant fight, finally succumbed to his attackers.

Sound Up Scheepers
And I think that’s where they strangled him. And he was pulled with this piece of nylon cord, he was dragged over here. His body lay like this. He was fastened here…

Derek: With the rope?

Scheepers: ja, with the rope against this piece of fence here. This whole place was full of blood here. He had a small… here you can see it, here’s the blood on the grass…

Derek: Still there hey…

Scheepers: That’s still Mr b’s blood.

Voice
Earlier this week a government delegation, including minister of police Bheki Cele, met with Horner’s family and several agricultural organisations. The minister has promised to look into the allegations of stock theft and police complicity, and vowed to return with a plan to reinforce rural safety within three weeks. For Scheepers, whose also had some of his farm workers attacked in recent months, that day can’t come fast enough.

Sound Up Scheepers
They beat up one of them, was in a coma I think for 5 months. All these bones, jawbone, cheekbones, there was not one single bone in tact. So it’s not only the white guys. If you run into those thieves at night, and you’re not prepared for them, you won’t make it.

Voice
This cross has been erected at the site of Brendin Horners death, another stark reminder of a country plagued by sadistic and often fatal farm attacks.


PART 1 ends





















PART 2

Friday’s protests in Senekal came after Commander in Chief of the Economic Freedom Fighters, Julius Malema, said the EFF would attend the bail hearing to protect state property after a group of farmers stormed the court at last week’s sitting, damaging court property and setting fire to a police vehicle. By thursday night tensions in town were running high with a heavy police presence already on scene.

Link Derek
Any doubts about the EFF arriving in force were dispelled early this morning, they were gathering in all parts of Senekal. Julius Malema has asked for a peaceful protest, but said they will retaliate if provoked. It’s really a wait and see situation.

Voice
A few hundred meters up the road was the designated staging point for groups like Afriforum and others.

Link Derek
But it seems that their mission is not to confront the EFF, but rather to show solidarity and their frustration with ongoing farm murders.

Voice
Kallie Kriel is the CEO of Afriforum.

Sound Up Kallie
Kallie: they are not going to bring solutions, so we will gain nothing by confronting them. What we will gain is to mobilise our people to look after their own safety.

Voice
Dr Theo de Jager is the chairman of the South African Agri Initiative, Saai. They say the issues around farm attacks in the country need to be solved urgently.

Sound Up Theo
We cannot just put Elastoplast on cancer, we must cut fast and deep, and make sure that we get to the root causes behind farm attacks and farm murders.

Voice
In between the two sides, another gathering took place. Senekal has become a flashpoint of combustible emotions around not only farm murders, but landlessness, poverty, hunger, corruption and crime that so many wanted to talk about …. Petrus Sitho, from East London, came clad in chains.

Sound Up Petrus Sitho
it represents that we don’t have freedom. They say that we’ve had freedom for 26 years. 26 years of killing our farmers? 26 years of corruption?

Voice
Unofficial spokesperson of the divurgent grouping, Hein Marx, said they would enter town despite mounting fears of clashes between the opposing sides.

Sound Up Hein Marx
We don’t threaten anybody, we will go and show who we are, what we are, and what we stand for. We’re not looking for trouble, but we’re definitely not going to stand back.

Voice
Back in town we spoke to Eff National Spokesperson Vuyani Pambo.
Sound Up Vuyani
Vuyani: So we are here to defend our state, this is the government of the people, so we are going to defend it.

Derek: Vuyani, anger on both sides. What is the solution here?

Vuyani: We need to take our land back. Black people need to take their land back. Because all of this is caused by the tension that is caused by inequality by black people not having land.

Derek: I did stories two weeks ago about how people have been given land in the Free State and the farms have gone to rack and ruin.

Vuyani: When you are given land, you need to be supported, even the Afrikaners were supported by the state for them to be where they are.

Derek: What is your view of the ongoing farm murders?

Vuyani: It’s insignificant.

Derek: Insignificant?

Vuyani: Insignificant. It’s not a big number. It’s not something that should make national, you know, discourse. It’s like any other murder, its murder. It’s not farm murders. Why do you want to categorise it? Why do you want to categorise it differently, treat it specially,

Voice
The situation reached boiling point when members of the farming community and their supporters entered town.

Link Derek
So some rolled up barbed wire is now the border - the border between the EFF supporters and the farming groups and their allies, some of them bikers, who’ve come all the way from Cape Town. But things are getting very tense right now.

Voice
The heavy police presence just managed to keep the groups apart, although there were some light skirmishes.

Sound Up Derek
Derek: Why have they started throwing things and destroying property?

Eff man 1: But it’s not your property.

Eff man 2: You are asking too much, lets go.

Derek: Asking too much?

Voice
Biker Brent van Heerden runs a group called I Ride To Freedom, that came to take a stand against farm murders. And he had this message for President Ramaphosa.

Sound Up Brent
Derek: So what’s your message to the president?

Brent: Mr President, corruption has to stop. Because it’s causing all the problems in this country. You know a poor country is always going to have crime. We’ve got starving people, we’ve got unemployed people, and we’ve got a government that is completely corrupt. If corruption doesn’t stop, we are only going to get worse.

Voice
Amidst the chaos, the ANC also made an appearance.

Link Derek
And in the heat of Senekal, the ANC are here to show that they are not forgotten. In a side street maybe, and not quite in the same numbers as the EFF.

Voice
Meanwhile, things were quieter but no less dramatic at the Senekal magistrates court, which had been blocked off from the public.

Link Derek
In the midst of the protest, some people may have forgotten what today is all about. It’s the bail hearing of the two men accused of murdering young farmer Brendin Horner. Still in progress.

Voice
Police Minister Bheke Cele also attended the proceedings. The two accused, 32 year old Sekwetje Mahlamba and 44 year old Sekola Matlaletsa pleaded not guilty and the bail hearing has been postponed until next tuesday. Both men have been accused of stock theft before, and investigating officer Captain Gerhardus Myburgh testified that police found bloodstained clothing in Mahlamba’s house. Outside court, tensions had subsided by midday. But the Freedom Front Plus has since lodged a complaint with the South African Human Rights Commission against Julius Malema and EFF supporters for singing the song “kill the boer”.
.+

Sound Up EFF supporters
Kill the boer, kill the farmer.

Voice:
And on Friday night another suspect responsible for damaging court property two weeks ago was arrested and charged with attempted murder, public violence, arson, and malicious damage to property.






















Senekal Promos




Promo 1
We visit the farm where the body of 21 year old Brendin Horner was found tied to a pole, the senseless murder which has driven the farming community over the edge and sparked tensions in Senekal.

Promo 2
In Senekal opposing groups converged on the Magistrate’s court for the bail hearing of two murder suspects in the killing of young Brendin Horner…we probe lingering tensions fuelling the protests.

Promo 3
Two suspects arrested for the murder of young Brendin Horner enraged the farming community of Senekal – we witness their bail hearing and ask what’s being done to stem rural crime.
